one_line: Coordinates multi-provider business procurement with constrained agent actions and reversible holds.
what_it_does: Plans a Toronto office opening across furniture, networking, and facilities providers under budget and deadline constraints, with human approval and an audit trail.
leverage_rationale: Structured, shared capability access lets an agent compare providers, check inventory and availability, create reversible holds, and release them against the same business state; UI-driving could approximate this but less reliably.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT states six page-bound tools including search_products, check_inventory, check_service_availability, reserve_outcome_resources, and release_outcome_reservations.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows a Toronto office procurement plan, supplier rows, budget, readiness, and a Human Control approval panel.
Frame sheets show the structured project and provider workflow, though repeated small frames do not clearly prove end-to-end completion.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent multi-provider workflow with approval, holds, release, shared domain logic, and audit trail, but visual evidence is repetitive and no transcript or submitted video is available.
execution_evidence: ABOUT describes a 15-person Toronto office scenario with CAD 12,000 budget and Friday deadline.
ABOUT claims UI and WebMCP use the same domain logic and state.
Devpost screenshot shows the plan and approval surface.
impact_rationale: Operations teams have a concrete procurement coordination problem involving constraints, provider availability, and authorization; the demonstrated workflow credibly reduces coordination risk.
impact_evidence: ABOUT specifies a concrete office-opening use case with three provider types and hard constraints.
Visible packaging shows supplier, quantity, subtotal, readiness, and approval information.
creativity_rationale: Reversible, auditable outcome holds and composable provider capabilities are a fresh application of WebMCP to business operations.
creativity_evidence: ABOUT emphasizes reversible holds, provider coordination, human approval, and visible provenance.
Experimental same-origin and cross-origin capability exposure is described.
usability_note: The approval-oriented procurement dashboard appears understandable, though small frame sheets limit assessment of interaction quality.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; frame sheets are repetitive and hard to read.
standouts: Reversible holds and explicit human control make agent authority concrete.
advance_reason: Strong agent-centered procurement concept with credible structured-state leverage and coherent packaging despite limited visual evidence.

one_line: Human-approved continuity ledger reconciles stale business information before publication or transaction.
what_it_does: Separates recovered sources, conflicts, approvals, published passport data, and transactions for a fictional Ugandan coffee supplier.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides bounded inspection and proposal capabilities over live ledger/passport state while withholding accept and publish authority; a general agent scraping UI cannot match the typed provenance and permission boundary as reliably.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes Ledger tools for conflict counts and source-backed proposals, and Passport tools preserving destination qualifications.
Frame sheets visibly show source discrepancies, Continuity Ledger records, proposed facts, and human decision controls.
Devpost screenshot shows the stale-information warning and coffee supplier context.
execution_rationale: The packet coherently covers Recover, Reconcile, Approve, Publish, and Transact, with visible conflict handling and separation between agent proposals and human publication; no video transcript limits certainty.
execution_evidence: ABOUT explicitly defines five visible stages and four disagreeing recovered records.
Frames show discrepancy cards, accepted status, ledger, and structured supplier records.
Human-only acceptance/publication is described consistently across surfaces.
impact_rationale: Stale contact, order, destination, and certification data create real operational and reputational risk for businesses; the workflow directly addresses safe continuity.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies concrete stale claims affecting a Ugandan coffee supplier.
Frames visibly show conflicting phone, minimum-order, Japan availability, and certification information.
creativity_rationale: The distinction between agent-ready data and trustworthy current data, embodied as a continuity ledger and human-controlled passport, is an original and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The central thesis that agent-ready stale information remains stale is explicit.
Frames show source separation, proposals, acceptance, and publication as distinct states.
usability_note: The staged ledger and review cards appear legible and actionable, though the dense evidence workflow may require onboarding.
red_flags: No submitted video/transcript; visual evidence is a storyboard-like contact sheet.
standouts: Strong human/agent authority boundary and source-backed continuity model.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-value human-in-the-loop continuity workflow with strong visual and textual coherence.

one_line: WebMCP-native live UI debugging measures runtime truth and stages safe source fixes.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect a human-selected live element, measure computed styles and contrast, preview Tailwind alternatives, and apply an undoable source edit only after human approval.
leverage_rationale: The product exposes browser-tab-only state—selection, computed cascade, design scale, live hover state, and HMR-linked source identity—that screenshots, repositories, APIs, and ordinary UI driving cannot comparably provide.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly says measurements are live runtime truth and unavailable from screenshots or repositories.
Transcript demonstrates analysis, staged alternatives, live morphing, human Apply boundary, HMR reconnect, undo, and hover-state holding.
ABOUT describes page-bound WebMCP tools returning state unique to the current tab.
execution_rationale: The 109-second video transcript demonstrates a complete central loop from vague complaint through measurement, preview, approval, real source update, HMR reconnection, undo, and reset.
execution_evidence: Video transcript details measured 13px padding vs 20px, corner mismatch, and contrast issue.
Transcript reports exact source update, HMR reconnect, undo, hover hold, and reset demo.
Facts confirm a live 109-second video and alive demo.
impact_rationale: Frontend developers and AI-assisted coding workflows have a concrete recurring problem—agents cannot access runtime visual truth—and Askew directly reduces diagnosis and correction errors.
impact_evidence: Transcript frames the screenshot-and-guess limitation in everyday AI-generated interface work.
Demonstrated metrics and safe apply flow address diagnosis and implementation together.
creativity_rationale: Pointing at a live element and speaking a vague complaint, then exposing held interaction state and measured cascade to an agent, is a novel and deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Live DOM selection and hover state are treated as first-class agent-readable state.
Human click is the sole write boundary while agent previews real component variants.
usability_note: Two sentences and two clicks form a clear workflow; staged previews and undo support safe use.
standouts: Exceptional WebMCP indispensability grounded in live browser-only state.
advance_reason: The strongest packet: video proves a coherent product and WebMCP changes what the agent can know and do.

one_line: Masks sensitive contract data locally with deterministic identifiers before AI review.
what_it_does: Detects and replaces personal data using regex and jurisdiction-specific checksums, keeps text in-browser, and restores values after processing.
leverage_rationale: Page-bound tools can transform the document without passing it as an argument, preserving the core local-privacy invariant; the same workflow could otherwise be performed with local UI automation but less safely and transparently.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT states the agent called mask_document_in_page with no document argument.
ABOUT describes deterministic local detection and restoration with no LLM receiving the contract.
Devpost packaging visibly contrasts what the human sees with what leaves the page.
execution_rationale: The concept and technical safeguards are coherent, but there is no video and the packet provides only limited visual proof of the complete mask/restore workflow.
execution_evidence: ABOUT lists coverage for IBAN, cards, Spanish DNI/NIE/CIF, Italian VAT, names, and contact data.
Packaging screenshot shows the no-argument in-page tool call and data boundary.
No frame sheets were submitted despite listed paths, and no transcript exists.
impact_rationale: EU legal and accounting users have a concrete privacy barrier to using AI on contracts; local deterministic masking directly addresses that high-stakes need.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies law firms and accountants across the EU and GDPR/AI Act sensitivity.
The product explicitly prevents contract text from leaving the browser before AI use.
creativity_rationale: Using verified jurisdiction-specific checksums and a reversible local masking boundary is a thoughtful, technically specific approach to safe AI document workflows.
creativity_evidence: ABOUT names ISO 13616, Luhn, Spanish DNI/NIE/CIF, and Italian VAT algorithms.
The no-argument page tool encodes privacy into the interaction model.
usability_note: The privacy promise is clear, but the packet does not establish how users review masking errors or handle ambiguous detections.
red_flags: No video or frame-sheet evidence; execution claims rely mainly on description and one packaging screenshot.
standouts: Strong local-privacy constraint with deterministic validation rather than LLM redaction.
advance_reason: High-impact privacy workflow and credible technical design; advance with execution confidence reduced for thin evidence.

one_line: Negotiates structured supplier offers while dynamically enforcing human transaction authority.
what_it_does: Discovers suppliers, compares constraints, negotiates quotes, verifies delivery, and exposes purchase capability only after exact human approval.
leverage_rationale: Authorization changes the actual WebMCP tool surface: purchase is absent before approval, appears for the exact supplier after approval, then is removed after ordering and replaced with status. This is materially beyond UI driving.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT reports 15 tools pre-approval, 16 after approval with bravo.create_purchase_order, and 16 ordered with get_order_status replacing purchase.
ABOUT specifies structured supplier contexts and constraint-aware negotiation.
Frame sheets visibly show procurement comparison, offer details, and approval/order states.
execution_rationale: The central negotiation and capability-lifecycle story is coherent and technically specific, with a stated live Chrome/WebMCP verification; missing video limits observed completion credit.
execution_evidence: ABOUT gives deterministic supplier outcomes and explains rejection of cheaper but late offer.
ABOUT documents pre-approval, approved, and ordered tool inventories.
Frames show repeated procurement workflow states and result panels.
impact_rationale: Procurement teams have real constraint and authorization problems; the product credibly helps compare offers while preventing agents from executing unapproved purchases.
impact_evidence: ABOUT specifies quantity, $2,500 budget, Friday deadline, and no-substitution constraints.
Visible frames show supplier offers, delivery constraints, and human approval.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic capability registration/removal tied to authorization and transaction lifecycle is an unusually strong WebMCP interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: Purchase capability existence is used as a permission primitive, not merely hidden behind a modal.
The workflow rejects the lowest price when it violates the actual delivery constraint.
usability_note: Constraint summary and explicit approval appear clear; negotiation complexity could be demanding for casual users.
red_flags: No submitted video/transcript; evidence is description plus contact sheets.
standouts: Capability lifecycle is a concrete, memorable permission boundary.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and creativity with a credible procurement result and authority model.

one_line: Fills high-stakes applications while enforcing human-only attestations in code.
what_it_does: Classifies fields as agent-fillable, human-only, or evidence-required; supports proposals, provenance, conditional sections, and hash-chained replayable history.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP tool availability and structured errors enforce field-level authority and conditional branches, preventing agents from touching attestations rather than merely warning in the UI.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT says answer_question on human-only fields returns a structured handoff error.
Evidence-required fields accept only propose_answer pending human confirmation.
ABOUT describes conditional tool existence and hash-chained mutation history.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete long-form branching application, provenance, blocked attestations, proposals, and review, but no video or transcript demonstrates the full run.
execution_evidence: ABOUT defines three permission classes and corresponding behaviors.
ABOUT describes self-employment branch revealing additional fields.
Frame sheets reportedly show application/review states, though visual details are limited.
impact_rationale: Visa, residency, and other high-stakes paperwork has a clear audience and real need for transcription assistance without unauthorized attestation.
impact_evidence: ABOUT gives concrete address, employment, date, attestation, and bank-balance examples.
The human-only signing boundary directly addresses consequential paperwork risk.
creativity_rationale: Permission-classed form fields, conditional capability surfaces, provenance, and replayable hash chains are a thoughtful interaction model for agent-assisted paperwork.
creativity_evidence: Attestation is treated as categorically different from transcription.
Conditional branches change what fields/tools exist based on answers.
usability_note: Structured permissions and review should improve trust, though a long branching application may be cognitively heavy.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; full workflow is not visually established.
standouts: Hard-coded authority boundary for attestations rather than a cosmetic warning.
advance_reason: High-impact, technically credible safety boundary for consequential forms, with strong leverage despite limited visual evidence.

one_line: Scores product ideas against evidence before founders commit to engineering.
what_it_does: Provides guided validation, reports, comparisons, methodology, settings, and an activity log with seven page-bound agent tools and explicit BUILD/VALIDATE/PIVOT/KILL outcomes.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured workspace and native tools improve repeatability and provenance for agent-assisted validation, but a general agent could achieve much of the same result with UI interaction.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT says seven native page-bound tools connect the agent to the same workspace.
ABOUT separates confidence from Build Score and preserves provenance.
Frame sheets visibly show a validation workspace and dashboard-style evidence surfaces.
execution_rationale: The product scope and outcomes are coherent, but the packet is text-heavy with no video and limited readable visual evidence, so end-to-end completeness is only plausible.
execution_evidence: ABOUT lists guided validation, reports, comparisons, methodology, settings, and activity log.
ABOUT names four explicit outcomes and seven tools.
Devpost screenshot/frames show a structured workspace but not a clearly completed validation run.
impact_rationale: Founders and AI-assisted builders have a real problem of building before validating; evidence-first decisions can prevent wasted engineering effort.
impact_evidence: ABOUT explicitly frames premature SaaS construction as the target problem.
Scoring dimensions include demand, pain, willingness to pay, distribution, competition, simplicity, and defensibility.
creativity_rationale: Evidence-first product validation with explicit build/pivot/kill decisions is a useful synthesis, though the category and scoring workflow are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Confidence is kept separate from score and provenance is preserved.
Mock-first with optional adapters and explicit consent is a thoughtful product stance.
usability_note: Guided stages and explicit outcomes suggest good usability; the packet does not show enough detail to assess friction.
red_flags: ABOUT contains noisy scraped formatting; no video/transcript; central workflow not shown end-to-end.
standouts: Separating evidence confidence from the recommendation score.
advance_reason: Clear founder pain point and credible workspace concept, but thin execution evidence lowers confidence and score.

one_line: Lets browser agents search, restyle, curate, and export a large open-source icon library in shared live state.
what_it_does: Provides icon discovery, filtering, styling, collections, and multi-format export through page-specific WebMCP tools while showing every agent action in the UI.
leverage_rationale: The agent can operate the same icon search, preview, collection, and styling state the human is watching, reducing hallucinated SVGs and inconsistent icon selection; still approximable by general UI driving.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes 16 tools across search, icon pages, collections, and dashboard.
ABOUT says search fills the visible search box, restyling changes the visible preview, and collection additions land in the visible grid.
Frame sheets show icon-library and collection/styling interfaces.
execution_rationale: The mature icon library, multiple export formats, page-specific tools, and visible shared-state behaviors present a complete product scope; lack of video limits direct proof of agent invocation.
execution_evidence: ABOUT claims 337,000+ icons from 239 sets and exports to SVG, React, Vue, Svelte, SwiftUI, Xcode catalogs, and PNG.
Facts report alive demo and four gallery images.
Frames show repeated search/icon/collection views.
impact_rationale: App developers and designers have a common need for consistent icon discovery and export; the product directly addresses agent-generated icon quality and curation friction.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies app builders as the audience and the problem of made-up or inconsistent icons.
Visible packaging communicates search, preview, style, and collection workflows.
creativity_rationale: Agent-visible icon curation and live art direction is a fresh extension of an established icon library, with solid depth across styling and export.
creativity_evidence: Two doors—editor MCP and in-site WebMCP—are presented.
The agent uses the same page the human is viewing rather than a hidden backend.
usability_note: Familiar search, preview, styling, and collection interactions with visible changes should be approachable.
red_flags: ABOUT says the library launched before the challenge, though WebMCP became the main feature of a release; origin eligibility depends on challenge rules.
standouts: Large real library plus live agent art direction and multi-format export.
advance_reason: Strong, usable creative/dev workflow with meaningful shared-state leverage; flag pre-existing origin for eligibility review.

one_line: Coordinates tenant repair cases from SMS intake through approved contractor booking.
what_it_does: Gathers safety/access facts, follows stored contractor agreements, obtains manager approval, confirms a time, books the visit, and texts the tenant.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools operate on a shared repair record and deliberately omit manager approval, letting the agent prepare work while code prevents unauthorized consequential booking; general UI automation is less reliable.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes twelve typed tools over the same workflow API and repair record.
ABOUT identifies manager approval as the intentionally absent WebMCP capability and server-enforced booking gate.
Video facts confirm a 135-second submitted video; frame sheets show repair workflow screens.
execution_rationale: The recorded controlled-live run covers intake, triage, manager approval, contractor disclosure/confirmation, booking, and tenant notification, with a resettable synthetic judge path.
execution_evidence: ABOUT gives an end-to-end controlled-live sequence from MMS through confirmed booking and tenant text.
Facts report a 135-second titled video and alive status unknown.
Frames visibly show case/dashboard and approval workflow states.
impact_rationale: Tenants, property managers, and contractors have a concrete high-friction repair coordination problem; the workflow credibly reduces repetition while preserving approval and safety.
impact_evidence: ABOUT describes fragmented conversations, safety/access details, prices, availability, approvals, and confirmations.
End-to-end run demonstrates value for all three participants.
creativity_rationale: Combining SMS/MMS intake, stored contractor agreements, agent preparation, fixed disclosure, and human authorization into one repair flow is an ambitious, memorable application.
creativity_evidence: The absent approval tool and server gate encode authority in the workflow.
Contractor must press 1 after disclosure before audio reaches OpenAI.
usability_note: Keeping tenants in SMS while giving managers a shared case is a strong usability choice; the multi-party flow remains operationally complex.
red_flags: Public judge URL is synthetic/resettable and demo_alive is unknown; controlled-live evidence is described rather than independently observed here.
standouts: End-to-end consequential workflow with explicit approval and voice safety boundary.
advance_reason: High-impact, complete repair workflow with strong WebMCP permission design and submitted video evidence.

one_line: Visualizes sugar and calorie intake while human and agent edit the same local daily log.
what_it_does: Tracks drinks and foods with flexible quantities, distinguishes sugar variants, converts grams to cube estimates, and synchronizes daily/monthly views locally.
leverage_rationale: Focused tools make searching, adding, updating, and removing validated entries in shared state convenient and repeatable, but a competent agent can drive the simple UI comparably with moderate friction.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT lists five tools for get_day, catalog search, add, update, and remove.
ABOUT says selected date, daily log, headline total, and calendar synchronize.
No frame sheets were submitted; one packaging screenshot is the main visual evidence.
execution_rationale: The described tracker has a coherent feature set and live demo, but no video or frame-sheet evidence demonstrates the central agent-assisted workflow end-to-end.
execution_evidence: ABOUT specifies flexible amounts, regular/diet/zero alternatives, custom labels, cube estimates, calories, and local storage.
Facts report alive demo and one gallery image.
Frame sheets are explicitly NONE SUBMITTED.
impact_rationale: People tracking sugar and calories have a clear everyday need for understandable portions and flexible logging; the product offers credible informational value without claiming medical advice.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies difficulty visualizing label grams and varied serving/portion behavior.
Features include sugar cubes, calories, flexible quantities, and monthly pattern highlights.
creativity_rationale: The sugar-cube visualization and shared human-agent tracker are useful new angles on a familiar nutrition-log category.
creativity_evidence: ABOUT describes cube estimates and regular/diet/zero distinctions.
Local, account-free page-bound agent editing is a practical interaction choice.
usability_note: Visual cubes, flexible portions, and local no-account use suggest approachable everyday logging.
red_flags: No submitted frame sheets or video; health-related usefulness is informational and self-entered, not clinically validated.
standouts: Clear sugar visualization and synchronized local state without account friction.
advance_reason: Coherent niche tracker, but WebMCP delta is modest and execution evidence is too thin relative to stronger packets.
